judgments.reason: The span 'lichenoid plaques on the right angle of mouth, bilateral buccal mucosa' appears literally in the vignette and documents mucosal involvement, supporting the 'mucocutaneous' modifier of lichen planus.

The span 'erosions covered with hemorrhagic crusts on the upper and lower lips' appears literally in the vignette and documents additional mucosal/cutaneous lip involvement, supporting the 'mucocutaneous' modifier.

The span 'painful swelling of the proximal nail folds' appears literally in the vignette and documents cutaneous/nail unit involvement, supporting the 'mucocutaneous' modifier alongside the mucosal findings.
The span 'violaceous discoloration of 7 fingernails and 3 toenails' appears literally in the vignette and documents nail (cutaneous) involvement consistent with the 'mucocutaneous' modifier.

The span 'longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation of the nail plate' appears literally in the vignette and documents nail unit changes characteristic of lichen planus, supporting the 'mucocutaneous' modifier.

The span 'partial to complete loss of nail plate with oozing of blood resulting in hemorrhagic crusting of the nail beds and folds' appears literally in the vignette and documents severe nail involvement, supporting the 'mucocutaneous' modifier.
